name: Low-Dimensional Antipodal Criterion for Learning-Space Graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a finite partial cube of isometric dimension at most three whose medium admits a closed orientation. Then $G$ is a learning-space graph if and only if $G$ contains an antipodal pair. Consequently, a finite convex subgraph $C$ of a learning-space graph with $\operatorname{idim}(C)\le3$ is a learning-space graph exactly when it contains a $C$-antipodal pair. The dimension bound is sharp: the semicube $\mathcal F_4\subseteq\mathcal P_4$ is a dimension-four counterexample.
proof: A learning-space graph has an antipodal pair by the defect-hitting theorem. Conversely, a closed orientation gives a well-graded union-closed positive-content family. In dimensions at most three, an antipodal pair forces either the empty state to be present or a translation by one member to be union closed; the rooted-union criterion then supplies a valid root. Convex restrictions inherit a closed parent orientation, while $\mathcal F_4$ proves sharpness.
